notes.summary: New positive concentration measures and exact bounded-oscillation/deep-tail split characterize J for every eligible measure.
notes.detailedSummary: Every concentration cluster has mass J and support in intersection of closures of exceptional opens. Exact A+/Q- and A-/Q+ sums equal J; if mu(N)=0, J is precisely the persistent negative-tail integral. Gives a positive cluster split and J-K Borel identity. Neither full-dual null annihilation nor uniform integrability is proved; the bump example is diagnostic only.
notes.text:
New universal concentration and truncation deductions use only earlier own note n1 and its explicit analytic-foundation boundary. Fix ANY eligible arbitrary-support mu and ANY fast actual maximizing sequence. Put v_n=-a_n, v=-u, d_n=(v_n-v)+, k_n=(v-v_n)+, changing u only on its mu-null pole set for integrals. Then int k_n mu->0, int d_n mu->J and int v_n mu->int v mu+J.

Every weak cluster zeta of the positive Radon measures d_n mu has mass J and support in A=intersection closure(O_m); every weak cluster of v_n mu is v mu+zeta. Existence follows by Tychonoff compactness of all bounded continuous-test coordinates and compact-Hausdorff Riesz. Integrable Borel densities of a finite Radon measure are Radon by truncation/simple approximation and regularity. The identity v_n mu-v mu=d_n mu-k_n mu proves cluster correspondence because the negative term tends to zero in total variation. For fixed m, d_n<=2^(1-n) off O_m, hence its integral there tends to0 and its integral on O_m tends toJ. Continuous tests supported outside closure(O_m), Urysohn/regularity and countable union give support in A. No support in N, uniqueness, singularity or exclusion of full points in A is claimed. J=0 iff v_n mu->v mu in total variation iff it converges weakly to that measure: the norm tends toJ, and the constant test proves the converse.

For T>0 set b_n^T=(min(v_n,T)-min(v,T))+, q_n(T)=int(v_n-T)+mu, q(T)=int(v-T)+mu. EXACTLY int_N b_n^T mu+q_n(T)->J+q(T). Proof: the opposite truncated part c_n^T is at most k_n, while b_n^T-c_n^T=v_n-v-(v_n-T)++(v-T)+. Integrate; off N, actual pointwise convergence and the bound b_n^T<=T give dominated convergence. Let A_T^+/A_T^- be limsup/liminf of the bounded integral on N and Q_T^+/Q_T^- those of q_n(T). Bounded parts increase with T, tails decrease, and the preceding sum bounds them. Their finite limits satisfy A^++Q^-=J and A^-+Q^+=J, since q(T) decreases to0.

If mu(N)=0, EVERY fixed-T ordinary limit exists: lim_n q_n(T)=J+q(T). Thus J=lim_T lim_n int(-a_n-T)+mu, and J=0 iff {-a_n} is uniformly integrable. In general J=0 iff uniform integrability AND every bounded truncation min(v_n,T) converges to min(v,T) in L1(mu). Uniform integrability is equivalent to lim_T limsup_n q_n(T)=0; finitely many early integrable terms allow replacement by sup_n. Truncated L1 convergence is equivalent to A^+=0 since c_n^T tends to0 and b_n^T vanishes off N. The exact identities prove the criterion. Full-dual finiteness has not been shown to supply these antecedents.

Each concentration cluster also splits zeta=eta+gamma, eta absolutely continuous to mu and zero off N, gamma positive supported in A. Refine its subnet simultaneously for b_n^T mu at integer T. The limits eta_T increase, are <=zeta and <=T mu|N, because the bounded integrals off N vanish. Their finite increasing Radon limit eta exists by countable monotone convergence and total variation approximation; gamma=zeta-eta. No subnet independence is asserted.

A diagnostic scalar example proves the measure-theoretic limitation: on[0,1] take disjoint I_n=(2^-n,2^-n+2^-2n) and triangular continuous bumps of height2^(2n+1), zero off I_n. Their integrals are1 and they tend to0 at every point, yet v_n dx->delta_0 by uniform continuity. O_m=union_(n>=m)I_n has empty intersection but intersection of closures{0}, and int(v_n-T)+->1. This is not an actual C/psh/maximizer counterexample to P16.7.

Both Borel moments are finite and int u nu=p, so subtraction gives J-K=int u(mu-nu). Equality J=K needs equality of those moments. Also u<=R<=0 implies R integrable and e-intR mu=B-J-int(R-u)mu; this assigns neither E(R) nor MA(R). Complete proofs are in new-residual-proofs.tex and standalone.tex. General J vanishing and analytic representation remain open.

notes.text:
New bounded-attainment and invariant-variation deductions use only earlier own note n1 at its declared analytic-foundation boundary. General attainment is not proved.

If an actual normalized q in C attains D(mu)=B, EVERY fast maximizing sequence satisfies I(a_n,q)<=4epsilon_n. Energy and weak-test moduli give e=E(q), nu=MA(q); full-point atoms give ell=q at every full point. The all-affinoid Shilov formula then gives R=q: the boundary maximum is at least the local q value, while continuity and affinoid neighborhoods inside arbitrarily small ordinary neighborhoods give the reverse inequality after infimizing. Consequently u<=q and s=intu mu<=intq mu=E(q)-B=r. Earlier s>=r forces J=0 and u=q mu-almost everywhere. Fixed bounded-MA L1 limits of a_n are both q, by the I modulus, and u, by the fast tails; hence they agree. Mixed measures are dominated by twice a midpoint MA measure. Global all-point C/G recognition of u, and generally mu=MA(q), do not follow from this argument.

An attained invariant slice DOES identify the equation. Suppose q(x)=qbar(tau(x)) is smooth periodic with I_2+Hess(qbar) positive definite everywhere, and q attains the full dual for an eligible arbitrary-support mu. Put lambda=MA(q). Coordinate dimension and identity calibration give lambda supported on the Gauss section with raw density2det(I_2+Hess(qbar))dr_1dr_2. For every smooth periodic h, compactness supplies a uniform positive Hessian bound for q and a finite Hessian bound for h. Thus q+t h(tau) is in the actual smooth CLD class for both signs of sufficiently small t. First variation at the maximum gives int h(tau)(lambda-mu)=0. Smooth periodic convolution proves density in continuous torus tests, so tau_*lambda=tau_*mu.

For every a in C, a(x)<=a(Gauss(tau(x))). Projection equality and skeletal support of lambda give int a mu<=int a lambda. Conversely the ACTUAL segment (1-t)q+ta has nonpositive right derivative at the maximum: int(a-q)(lambda-mu)<=0. Projection equality gives intq(lambda-mu)=0, so the opposite inequality holds. Equality on C and density of its real span give equality of the actual finite Radon measures. This uses no positivity margin for arbitrary smooth perturbations.

In particular, on the ENTIRE eligible arbitrary-support class, D(mu)=0 iff mu=theta^2. If D(mu)=0, q=0 attains the dual and has coordinate Hessian I_2, so the preceding proof applies. Conversely tangent concavity at0 gives D(theta^2)=0. Skeletal support is forced as a conclusion on this slice, not imposed on the input. This supplies no every-measure attainment or existence theorem.
